$schema_note: Durable, shared state file fix #5 introduces: harness/stack-state.json on disk, one entry per app_context ever planned. Written by the executor only after the verification gate (fix #4) actually passes -- never speculatively. Read by the planner before it falls back to live Floci discovery.
why_this_exists: Live Floci-state inspection (what fix-1/fix-2's planners already do) gets ordinary incrementality right when there's exactly one app's resources on the instance -- verified in the baseline and fix-1/fix-2 runs. It breaks down once MULTIPLE apps share the same Floci instance with plausibly-similar resource names (a realistic scenario for a hackathon demo box or a shared dev environment): live discovery alone has no reliable way to know which existing bucket is 'this app's' photo storage versus a different app's. The state file is keyed by app_context specifically to make that lookup exact instead of a semantic guess.

field_notes.top_level_keys: app_context strings -- must match exactly what the planner assigns/reuses; this is the only correct disambiguator between two apps whose resources happen to look similar.
field_notes.capabilities: Keyed by capability_id, one entry per capability ever successfully gated for that app.
field_notes.last_gate_result: Set from harness/verify_gate.py's actual output, never from an executor's self-report -- an entry only gets written/updated after a real PASS.
field_notes.staleness: A planner that finds an app_context here should still treat last_verified as a hint, not proof current -- re-running the gate (fix #4) before declaring anything ready is still required; this file records intent and history, not live truth.
